headline: Is he really who he says he is?
note: Only on the two Magician/Hanged Man/Fool decks, so one set of copy, verb swapped.

a: You turned the Magician, dear. Look — roses and lilies at his feet, and one arm held straight up.
You asked if he's really who he says he is. Your hand went to the man who builds what you see.
The Magician isn't a liar, dear. He's a maker.
What he shows you was put together on purpose.
That's not the same as false. But it isn't all of him.
You sensed a second man under the first one. Take that seriously.
Let me look closer at the man he leaves out…
b: You turned the Hanged Man, dear. Look — one leg tied to the branch, the other bent behind it, out of sight.
You asked if he's really who he says he is. Your hand went to the card of one hidden side.
The card doesn't say he's someone else, dear.
It says you have only ever seen one side of him.
That's why you can't get a clean read on him.
The trouble isn't your judgement, dear. It's what you were handed.
Let me look closer at the side he never showed you…
c: You turned the Fool, dear. Look — all he owns is tied in one small bundle on a stick.
You asked if he's really who he says he is. Your hand went to the man still deciding.
The Fool isn't pretending, dear. He hasn't finished choosing.
So the man you met and the man now are both him.
They just aren't the same one yet.
You keep noticing he doesn't add up. He doesn't yet — and you saw it.
Let me look closer at which of him is the one that stays…
